subject: Damages reciprocity, incidental/punitive definitions — Acme Order Form redlines
messages:
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Acme OF redline — consequential/incidental language (heads up)

Marissa / Karthik,

Acme pushed back on the limitation of liability section in the Order Form we circulated. They flagged the consequential damages exclusion and are arguing for one-way language that would favor them (they want us to accept mutuality but exclude certain categories only against them). Attached is the PDF of their proposed paragraph from Contracts Ops.

High-level: they do not want "incidental/special/consequential" to sweep in lost business or downstream claims tied to their customers. They asked us to either (A) accept a mutual exclusion with a confidentiality/data-breach carve-out, or (B) accept a one-way exclusion but with an increased cap for direct damages.

Can you please:
- Advise preferred legal position (mutual vs one-way, and whether typical carve-outs should include confidentiality/data loss or not)
- Propose neat redline language we can send back (ideally 1–2 short alternatives)
- Flag any internal commercial impacts we should surface to Sales/Finance (karthik, please chime in)

Attachments: Acme_Proposed_Ltd_Liability_20260901.pdf

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T11:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Acme OF redline — consequential/incidental language (legal view)

Dylan / Karthik,

Thanks — reviewed Acme's proposed text. High level guidance and two clean options below.

Background observation: "consequential"/"incidental"/"special"/"punitive" are often grouped; the battleground is (1) mutuality and (2) carve-outs for confidentiality, data loss, indemnity, and willful misconduct. Customers frequently push to carve out data/PII breaches from exclusions. We should avoid a one-way exclusion that leaves us exposed for large downstream business losses unless there is a compensating increase in the cap or a specific carve-out that limits exposure.

Option A — Mutual exclusion (recommended):
"Except to the extent arising from a party's (a) gross negligence, willful misconduct, (b) breach of confidentiality obligations, or (c) obligation to indemnify the other party, neither party shall be liable to the other for any special, indirect, incidental, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages, including lost profits and loss of business or revenue."

Option B — Customer-favorable compromise (commercial):
"Except for liability arising from a party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, or indemnification obligations, the Customer may recover direct damages up to the greater of (i) the fees paid to Vendor under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim or (ii) $1,000,000. Neither party shall be liable to the other for special, incidental, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages."

Notes:
- If Sales needs upside flexibility, we can propose a deal-specific uplift to the cap instead of moving to one-way language.
- Define "consequential" expansively (include "indirect, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data or use"), but keep carve-outs narrow and explicit.
- If Acme insists on one-way language, make that a commercial concession tied to an increased cap and specific carve-outs (e.g., cyber/data breach not excluded).

I attached a one-page redline with the two alternatives for quick sending: Redwood_proposed_redline_20260904.docx

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jamie.Torres@acmecorp.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acmecorp.com, marta.ruiz@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-09-03T14:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Damages language — Acme OF comments

Dylan,

Thanks for the transparency. Our position is driven by the downstream exposure Acme faces from product outages and data issues — we can't agree to broad one-way limits that cap our ability to recover meaningful consequential losses from vendors. That said, we're open to a practical middle ground.

Proposed from our side (redline excerpt):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data or loss of use; provided, however, that such exclusion shall not apply to (a) damages arising from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) damages resulting from a party's breach of its confidentiality obligations or unauthorized access to Customer Data, or (c) Customer's claims for loss of business arising from Vendor's failure to meet SLA commitments where such failure results in a prolonged outage exceeding 8 hours."

We believe the SLA carve-out is reasonable given the product is customer-facing for critical workflows. If Redwood wants mutuality, the SLA carve-out should apply to both parties. We can accept a mutual exclusion with that narrowly tailored SLA carve-out.

If you have a short alternative we can review today, please send it.

Best,
Jamie Torres
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp.
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Jamie.Torres@acmecorp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-04T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Damages language — Acme OF comments

Jamie — appreciate the quick reply and the SLA carve-out suggestion. Sending a short hybrid we can agree on internally; Marissa please confirm.

Proposed short compromise (for Acme review):
"Except for liability arising from (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) breach of confidentiality or unauthorized access to Customer Data, (iii) indemnification obligations, or (iv) damages directly resulting from a material and prolonged failure to meet the applicable SLA (an outage exceeding eight (8) consecutive hours), neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages, including lost profits and loss of business. For the avoidance of doubt, loss of Customer Data is excluded from the exclusion in clause (ii) above and remains actionable where caused by the Vendor's breach."

Commercial note to Acme: We are prepared to accept the SLA carve-out as mutual, but any one-way treatment (i.e., carving in consequentials only for Customer) would require increasing the direct damages cap to the greater of (i) 12 months' fees or (ii) $2,000,000. Karthik — please confirm whether Sales can support that uplift if Contract insists on a one-way outcome.

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_redline_20260904.docx

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jamie.Torres@acmecorp.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acmecorp.com, marta.ruiz@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-09-06T17:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Damages language — Acme OF comments (final)

Dylan / Marissa,

Appreciate the clarity — Acme legal reviewed the hybrid you proposed. We are prepared to accept the mutual language with the SLA carve-out as written, and we agree to the explicit confidentiality/data breach carve-out. We made a couple of minor clarifications to the SLA threshold and to the definition of "unauthorized access"; see attached pdf with comments.

Next steps:
- If Redwood is comfortable, let's lock the mutual language and move the Order Form to procurement for final signatures.
- If you're electing the one-way cap uplift instead, please return the revised cap number and we'll escalate internally.

Attachments: redline_final_comments_20260906.pdf

Regards,
Jamie Torres
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp.
